country.name: Nicaragua
country.languagePolicy: Spanish is the default interface language. Miskitu, Mayangna, Rama, Garífuna, English/Kriol and other Caribbean Coast language and cultural requirements require review with the autonomous-region authorities and affected communities; machine translation is not reviewed localization.

review.policy: No category becomes verified without a named qualified Nicaraguan reviewer, current authoritative sources and review of national, departmental, municipal, autonomous-region and institutional authority where applicable.

governanceModel.summary: Nicaragua combines MINED responsibility for basic, secondary and teacher education with territorial administration; Caribbean Coast autonomous-region and intercultural requirements; CNU coordination of higher education; and CNEA regulation, evaluation and accreditation quality categories.
governanceModel.territorialRule: Record department, municipality, modality and autonomous-region or community authority where applicable.
governanceModel.higherEducationRule: Preserve CNEA's exact institution category and accreditation or verification status; CNU membership, legal establishment, verification and accreditation are not interchangeable.

authorities.name: Ministerio de Educación
authorities.role: national authority for basic, secondary and teacher education, curriculum, centers and statistics

authorities.name: Consejo Nacional de Universidades
authorities.role: higher-education coordination within its legal competence

authorities.name: Consejo Nacional de Evaluación y Acreditación
authorities.role: national education quality assurance, evaluation and accreditation authority

authorities.name: Asamblea Nacional de Nicaragua
authorities.role: official legislation and consolidated legal sources

authorities.name: Ministerio de la Familia, Adolescencia y Niñez
authorities.role: child and adolescent protection and information system

curriculum.title: Documentos curriculares y mallas curriculares
curriculum.implementationRule: Confirm level, grade, modality, pedagogical unit, publication version and current MINED guidance, including bilingual-bicultural provisions in autonomous regions.
curriculum.supplementPolicy: External resources may supplement but never silently replace controlling MINED plans, programs and curricular guidance.

schoolDirectory.primarySourceName: Mapa Interactivo de Educación Básica, Media y Formación Docente
schoolDirectory.scopeNotice: The map supplies georeferenced center data and indicators. BRASA must preserve department, municipality, modality, indicator period and update date and must not infer current authorization of every program from location alone.

educationStatistics.scopeNotice: Every figure must display indicator definition, geographic level, reporting period, update date and source. Historical figures cannot be presented as current.

higherEducation.qualityAuthority: Consejo Nacional de Evaluación y Acreditación
higherEducation.authorityNotice: CNEA publishes distinct categories and verification status. A listing, CNU membership or legal establishment does not by itself prove current institutional or program accreditation.

privacyAndSafeguarding.dataProtectionLaw: Ley No. 787, Ley de Protección de Datos Personales
privacyAndSafeguarding.scopeNotice: Current consolidated law, regulations, enforcement authority, sensitive learner data, cross-border processing, consent, safeguarding and incident procedures require qualified review before real learner participation.

completionCriteria: A qualified Nicaraguan education reviewer is named.
MINED national, departmental, municipal and autonomous-region boundaries are reviewed.
Every school record preserves level, modality, geography, reporting period and source date.
Every statistic shows definition, geography, period, update date and provenance.
Every higher-education record preserves CNEA's exact category, decision, verification or accreditation status and effective period.
Curriculum mappings identify level, grade, modality, pedagogical unit and publication version.
Caribbean Coast language, cultural and autonomous-region requirements are reviewed with competent community participation.
Law 787's current consolidated text, regulations and enforcement arrangements are reviewed by qualified Nicaraguan counsel.
Privacy, child protection, accessibility, incident and consent procedures are approved by the participating institution.
No authorization, accreditation, partnership or credential claim exceeds documentary evidence.
